# Who Carries a Creative Vision Into Production? — complete editable platform copy

## 1. LONG VIDEO
Begin with the sentence “send it to production.” Expand it into specification, labor, sample, approval, money, change, shipment, quality, remedy, and archive. Use the public agreement only as one example; label every private arrangement unresolved until evidenced.

## 2. SHORT 01
“Production does not execute vision. People translate it.” Put a decision, a constraint, and a bearer of risk behind every transformation.

## 3. SHORT 02
“The purchase order is not the whole workplace.” Add employer, contractor, subcontractor, worker, jurisdiction, classification evidence, safety route, and payment record.

## 4. CAROUSEL
VISION / SPECIFICATION / PATTERN / SAMPLE / MATERIAL / LABOR / APPROVAL / CHANGE / PAYMENT / QUALITY / REMEDY / MEMORY.

## 5. NEWSLETTER
Subject: Who actually carries the vision into production? Offer a one-style trace and explain why a house must record uncertainty instead of implying supply-chain knowledge it does not possess.

## 6. PARTICIPANT REVIEW
Separate studio, supplier, and worker-facing review sheets so each party can correct role, timeline, decision, cost, safety, confidentiality, and unresolved disagreement.

## Claim ledger
- **VERIFIED:** U.S. Department of Labor garment-industry resources address federal wage, hour, recordkeeping, contractor, and compliance questions relevant to covered workplaces. (S76, S81)
- **VERIFIED:** The public Mossimo–Target agreement demonstrates one negotiated division among design, materials, approvals, manufacture, distribution, channels, and publicity. (S77)
- **INFERENCE:** Production handoffs distribute creative, technical, commercial, and labor power, but the distribution is not identical across houses, jurisdictions, or worker classifications. (S76, S77, S81)

## Publication discipline
Use the copy as written with the package's rendered social artwork. Preserve captions, alt text, creator and institution credits, canonical URLs, evidence labels, labor and jurisdiction limits, participant correction, and counsel or specialist boundaries.
